notes: Rounds of enemies walking one lane to a core while the player buys and places towers beside it is Strategy's Tower Defense, and the author's answer confirming a single lane makes lane-actor-track the shape; its P6 is not negotiable because the lane has to be one continuous valid route for the waves. SET rides alongside it because the player never sets foot in the map — they look down into it and drag towers onto allowed ground — so traversal and jump-gap checks have nothing to check, while the map, towers and enemies are still built as real parts exactly as asked. buildzone-grid is doing double duty as the allowed placement areas and, by contrast, the disallowed path, and I chose to keep it a compact single-view board on the grassy toy-soldier theme the author picked. The round-50-then-freestyle system, the coin shop and the drag radius indicator are all UI and gameplay rather than layout, so nothing in the map is routed for them; I left board-grid aside since the enemy lane, not a tile board, is what the space actually is.
